title: Popular Cities for Cybersecurity Jobs in 2026
summary: Cybersecurity is an attractive career for many reasons, including the number of cities with opportunities for cybersecurity professionals. Learn more about job roles to consider and the best cities for cybersecurity jobs across the country.
body_markdown:
## Key takeaways


-


Some of the best US cities for cybersecurity jobs are Huntsville, AL, San Jose, CA, Bloomington, IL, and Trenton, NJ.


-


Cybersecurity careers across the country give you an opportunity to protect networks, devices, and data for individuals, companies, and organizations.


-


Cybersecurity is in demand, with the rising incidence of data breaches and the market projected to reach $265.17 billion worldwide by 2030 \[[1](https://www.statista.com/outlook/tmo/cybersecurity/worldwide) \].


Types of cybersecurity jobs include information security analyst, security engineer, cryptographic engineer, and penetration tester. Discover some of the best cities for cybersecurity jobs and the types of jobs that may be available.


If you’re interested in starting a career in cybersecurity, consider the[Google Cybersecurity Professional Certificate](https://www.coursera.org/professional-certificates/google-cybersecurity) on Coursera. This nine-course series is designed ​​to help you find your first job in the field of cybersecurity, even with no previous experience, all at your own pace. Topics covered include identifying common risks, threats, and vulnerabilities, and learning techniques to mitigate them, protecting networks, devices, people, and data from unauthorized access and cyberattacks using SIEM tools, and getting hands-on experience with Python, Linux, and SQL.


###


## The importance of cybersecurity careers


[Cybersecurity](https://www.coursera.org/articles/what-is-cyber-security) is the practice of protecting networks, devices, and data to prevent access by individuals who should not have it. This practice ensures the confidentiality, validity, and availability of information.


In many people’s daily lives, technology is ever-present. This is the case, too, with organizations. Businesses often hold sensitive information that they are required by law to protect. Globally, the average cost of a data breach for a company reached $4.4M in 2025, according to IBM \[[2](https://www.ibm.com/reports/data-breach?utm_content=SRCWW&p1=Search&p4=43700077724063991&p5=e&gad_source=1&gclid=CjwKCAjwuJ2xBhA3EiwAMVjkVMKAdPVCi3j5RwwTj_beoLen5d0HGlo1wSpmZk67UDAljmd8KQypjhoCYWAQAvD_BwE&gclsrc=aw.ds#:~:text=can%20save%20millions-,USD%204.45%20million,-The%20global%20average) \]. Common[cybersecurity attacks](https://www.coursera.org/articles/types-of-cyber-attacks) include:


-


Malware


-


[Phishing](https://www.coursera.org/articles/types-of-phishing)


-


Man-in-the-middle


-


[Structured query language](https://www.coursera.org/articles/what-does-sql-stand-for) (SQL) injection


-


Zero-day exploits


-


Denial-of-service attacks, or DNS tunneling attacks


Each of these attacks involves attackers infiltrating a network, gaining unauthorized access to a two-party transaction, or preventing a system from working properly. Enterprises such as credit card companies, health care organizations, e-commerce companies, and many more rely on robust cybersecurity departments to protect information. With the rising incidence of[data breaches](https://www.coursera.org/articles/data-security-breach) , protecting that information is paramount. You can take part in building and maintaining security systems with a career in[cybersecurity](https://www.coursera.org/articles/how-to-get-into-cybersecurity) .


### How much do data breaches cost organizations?


The average data breach costs an organization $4.4 million, according to a 2025 report by IBM \[[2](https://www.ibm.com/reports/data-breach?utm_content=SRCWW&p1=Search&p4=43700077724063991&p5=e&gad_source=1&gclid=CjwKCAjwuJ2xBhA3EiwAMVjkVMKAdPVCi3j5RwwTj_beoLen5d0HGlo1wSpmZk67UDAljmd8KQypjhoCYWAQAvD_BwE&gclsrc=aw.ds#:~:text=can%20save%20millions-,USD%204.45%20million,-The%20global%20average) \]. That figure represents a 9 percent decrease from the previous year due to faster identification and containment, underscoring the importance of cybersecurity jobs \[[2](https://www.ibm.com/reports/data-breach?utm_content=SRCWW&p1=Search&p4=43700077724063991&p5=e&gad_source=1&gclid=CjwKCAjwuJ2xBhA3EiwAMVjkVMKAdPVCi3j5RwwTj_beoLen5d0HGlo1wSpmZk67UDAljmd8KQypjhoCYWAQAvD_BwE&gclsrc=aw.ds#:~:text=can%20save%20millions-,USD%204.45%20million,-The%20global%20average) \].


### Types of cybersecurity jobs


Cybersecurity professionals typically specialize in different functions, including building security systems, testing defense mechanisms, and responding to attacks. The scope of your work may include developing emergency response plans, processing and analyzing data, and testing systems to ensure they are compliant with laws and industry regulations. The following list shows common cybersecurity job titles and their associated median total salaries according to Glassdoor. These figures include base salary and additional pay, which may represent profit-sharing, commissions, bonuses, or other compensation:


-


[Information security analyst](https://www.coursera.org/articles/information-security-analysts-what-they-do) : $138,000


-


Digital forensic analyst: $133,000


-


IT security auditor: $116,000


-


Security systems administrator: $116,000


-


[Security engineer](https://www.coursera.org/articles/what-is-a-security-engineer) : $173,000


-


Cryptography engineer: $180,000


-


Cybersecurity manager: $183,000


-


Security architect: $233,000


-


[Penetration tester](https://www.coursera.org/articles/how-to-become-a-penetration-tester) : $155,000


## What are the best cities for cybersecurity jobs?


Cybersecurity is a growing profession with career opportunities available in cities across the US. Whether you’d like to work in a booming metropolis or a small to midsize community, cybersecurity could offer opportunities in your preferred area.


Explore some popular cities for cybersecurity jobs below, according to Glassdoor and BLS data, and CompTIA's[State of the Tech Workforce 2026](https://lecbyo.files.cmp.optimizely.com/download/ca5c4d84197d11f1b0fa326ff783616b) report.


### Small cities


#### Idaho Falls, ID


The second-largest city in Idaho outside of the Boise metro area has a lot to offer for cybersecurity professionals. Idaho Falls is a hub for commerce and[health care](https://www.coursera.org/articles/cyber-security-in-healthcare) in the eastern part of the state. Idaho National Laboratory and Eastern Idaho Regional Medical Center have headquarters in Idaho Falls, presenting opportunities for cybersecurity jobs.


#### Ithaca, NY


Ithaca, New York, is a small city with affluent prospects for cybersecurity professionals. This city is home to Cornell University and Ithaca College, two schools with respected[computer science programs](https://www.coursera.org/degrees/computer-science) .


### Medium cities


#### Bloomington, IL


Bloomington, a city about two hours from Chicago, is a hub for tech jobs. Companies such as State Farm Insurance and COUNTRY Financial are headquartered here, and 74.862 per 1,000 residents work in the tech sector \[[3](https://www.bls.gov/oes/2023/may/oes_14010.htm) \].


#### Huntsville, AL


Many companies (Invariant Corporation, Nippon Express, Torch Technologies, and more) call Huntsville home, opening opportunities for cybersecurity professionals. Additionally, the significant presence of military and[government](https://www.coursera.org/articles/cyber-security-jobs-in-government) contractors in Huntsville makes it an ideal center for IT careers. In 2025, employers posted 13,786 job postings requesting cybersecurity skills \[[6](https://lecbyo.files.cmp.optimizely.com/download/ca5c4d84197d11f1b0fa326ff783616b) \].


#### Trenton, NJ


New Jersey ranks number one in broadband connectivity, number five in fastest download speeds, and number one overall as the nation's best network performance and near-universal access, according to 2025 BroadbandNow data \[[4](https://broadbandnow.com/research/best-states-with-internet-coverage-and-speed) \]. A strong talent pool supports the cybersecurity industry in Trenton, with the prestigious Princeton University near the city and a high education level. Approximately 16 percent of Trenton’s workforce holds a bachelor’s degree or higher \[[5](https://www.census.gov/quickfacts/fact/table/trentoncitynewjersey/SBO050223) \]. Trenton hosts 733 tech companies, and 9,082 job postings asked for individuals with cybersecurity skills in 2025, according to CompTIA \[[6](https://lecbyo.files.cmp.optimizely.com/download/ca5c4d84197d11f1b0fa326ff783616b) \].


#### San Jose, CA


San Jose is the largest city in Silicon Valley, and tech jobs are plentiful, with 141.7 tech workers per 1,000 employees \[[7](https://www.bls.gov/oes/2023/may/oes_41940.htm#15-0000) \]. Silicon Valley is one of the country's most important hubs of technology innovation and entrepreneurship. This epicenter for IT careers has remained one of the top five areas for tech jobs, thanks to the thousands of start-up companies that operate here. Cybersecurity positions grew by 2 percent from 2025 to 2026 in San Jose \[[6](https://lecbyo.files.cmp.optimizely.com/download/ca5c4d84197d11f1b0fa326ff783616b) \].


#### Boulder, CO


Boulder has a median total annual salary of $102,000 for IT jobs, including base salary and additional pay, which may represent profit-sharing, commissions, bonuses, or other compensation \[[8](https://www.glassdoor.com/Salaries/boulder-information-technology-salary-SRCH_IL.0,7_IM110_KO8,30.htm) \]. The city supports technology-focused companies, with more than 19,000 tech workers living in the area \[[9](https://bouldereconomiccouncil.org/boulder-economy/key-industries-companies/itsoftware/) \]. Cisco, IBM, and Fanatics all chose to have locations in Boulder.


#### Austin, TX


Austin is a growing city that's highly ranked for its cost of living and wages for tech workers \[[6](https://lecbyo.files.cmp.optimizely.com/download/ca5c4d84197d11f1b0fa326ff783616b) \]. It's also home to a growing cybersecurity industry. Employers in Austin advertised 60,748 IT job postings in 2025, of which 40,053 asked for[cybersecurity skills](https://www.coursera.org/articles/cybersecurity-analyst-skills) \[[6](https://lecbyo.files.cmp.optimizely.com/download/ca5c4d84197d11f1b0fa326ff783616b) \]. IT jobs in Austin have a median salary of $99,000 yearly \[[10](https://www.glassdoor.com/Salaries/austin-it-salary-SRCH_IL.0,6_IM60_KO7,9.htm) \]. This figure includes base salary and additional pay, which may represent profit-sharing, commissions, bonuses, or other compensation.


###


### Is cybersecurity in demand?


Cybersecurity is a growing field, with an increasing amount of information being stored on digital devices in industries ranging from e-commerce to health care to credit card services. Revenue in the industry is likely to grow 5.79 percent between 2026 and 2030, reaching $265.17 billion worldwide by 2030 \[[1](https://www.statista.com/outlook/tmo/cybersecurity/worldwide) \].


### Large cities


#### Colorado Springs, CO


Colorado Springs is smaller than many other major tech hubs in the country, but with 53.56 tech employees per 1,000 workers, cybersecurity is among the top career options in the city \[[11](https://www.bls.gov/oes/2023/may/oes_17820.htm#15-0000) \]. While the western region of the US features some major cities for tech jobs, Colorado Springs is a midsize option that offers the possibility of a high salary and career growth. Cybersecurity jobs grew by 3.5 percent in Colorado Springs between 2025 and 2026 \[[6](https://lecbyo.files.cmp.optimizely.com/download/ca5c4d84197d11f1b0fa326ff783616b) \].


#### Washington, DC


The nation’s capital ranked second in total employment of tech professionals in 2026, with 35,058 cybersecurity skills job postings the year prior \[[6](https://lecbyo.files.cmp.optimizely.com/download/ca5c4d84197d11f1b0fa326ff783616b) \]. The Washington, DC, metropolitan area is home to many government agencies and technology companies, which employ 239,700 people in total \[[12](https://www.bls.gov/oes/2023/may/oes_47900.htm#15-0000) \].


#### Albuquerque, NM


Albuquerque is another smaller but high-powered city for tech careers. Albuquerque has 11,730 people working in tech jobs \[[13](https://www.bls.gov/oes/2023/may/oes_10740.htm#15-0000) \]. New Mexico’s largest city is also an excellent place for diversity in technology. CompTIA reports Albuquerque hosts 1,676 tech businesses, with 12,810 cybersecurity job postings and a 2.5 percent growth in cybersecurity jobs in 2025 \[[6](https://lecbyo.files.cmp.optimizely.com/download/ca5c4d84197d11f1b0fa326ff783616b) \].


#### Seattle, WA


Some of the biggest companies in the world, including Amazon, Starbucks, and Microsoft, base their operations in or next to Seattle. A great deal of Seattle’s workforce is in tech, with 82.64 employees per 1,000 working in this sector \[[14](https://www.bls.gov/oes/2023/may/oes_42660.htm#15-0000) \]. CompTIA reports that cybersecurity jobs increased 2.3 percent in 2025, and 50,698 job listings asked for cybersecurity skills \[[6](https://lecbyo.files.cmp.optimizely.com/download/ca5c4d84197d11f1b0fa326ff783616b) \]. Another popular spot for tech careers lies nearby, with Olympia, Washington, employing 6,360 tech employees \[[15](https://www.bls.gov/oes/2023/may/oes_36500.htm#15-0000) \].


#### San Francisco, CA


San Francisco, a major city near Silicon Valley, is one of the premier places for cybersecurity careers. Tech jobs in San Francisco totaled 334,428 in 2025, and the city ranks fifth in top metro areas by net tech employment, with 33,582 cybersecurity-related jobs \[[6](https://lecbyo.files.cmp.optimizely.com/download/ca5c4d84197d11f1b0fa326ff783616b) \]. The median total pay for tech workers in the area is $142,000 \[[16](https://www.glassdoor.com/Salaries/information-technology-salary-SRCH_IM759_KO0,22.htm) \]. This figure includes base salary and additional pay, which may represent profit-sharing, commissions, bonuses, or other compensation.


#### New York, NY


Among the largest cities in the world, New York City offers a great deal of opportunities in cybersecurity. New York is at the top of CompTIA’s rankings for tech employment, with 594,191 technology jobs in the city \[[16](https://www.comptia.org/content/research/state-of-the-tech-workforce) \] and 26,337 tech companies \[[6](https://lecbyo.files.cmp.optimizely.com/download/ca5c4d84197d11f1b0fa326ff783616b) \]. The city experienced a 2.9 percent increase in cybersecurity jobs in 2025, with 188,121 cybersecurity skills job postings \[[6](https://lecbyo.files.cmp.optimizely.com/download/ca5c4d84197d11f1b0fa326ff783616b) \]. Cybersecurity professionals can make attractive salaries in NYC, with the average tech worker earning around $111,000 annually \[[17](https://www.glassdoor.com/Salaries/new-york-city-information-technology-salary-SRCH_IL.0,13_IM615_KO14,36.htm) \]. This includes base salary and additional pay, which may represent profit-sharing, commissions, bonuses, or other compensation.


## How to begin your job search


The beginning of a job search is an ideal time to reflect on your values and aspirations. Considering your career goals, skills, and experience can help you choose an area to look for a job in.


### Decide on your ideal location and type of industry.


Finding the perfect city to call home involves a lot of thought and consideration. Each location you explore for a new job will include advantages and disadvantages. If you're planning to relocate for a cybersecurity job, keep the following factors in mind:


-


**Lifestyle:** Consider the size and feel of the city. Do you crave the energy and variety of a bustling metropolis or the peace and quiet of a small town? Suburbs offer a middle ground.


-


**Climate:** Do you prefer sunshine and warmth year-round or distinct seasons with cooler winters? Think about how the weather will affect your day-to-day life and outdoor hobbies.


-


**Activities and culture:** What are you passionate about? Does the city offer museums, theaters, and events that align with your interests? Are there opportunities for hiking, biking, or exploring nature?


-


**Cost of living:** Research housing costs, groceries, transportation, and taxes. Can you comfortably live on your expected income in this city?


-


**Commute:** How important is a short commute? When considering different areas, factor in public transportation options, traffic patterns, and average commute times.


**Read more:**[What Is a Good Salary?](https://www.coursera.org/articles/what-is-a-good-salary)


### Review your qualifications and skills.


Information security analysts typically hold[bachelor’s degrees](https://www.coursera.org/degrees/bachelors) in majors such as computer and information technology. A background in topics such as[engineering](https://www.coursera.org/collections/degrees-in-engineering) or mathematics can be helpful in cybersecurity jobs.


### Consider earning a certification.


[Certifications](https://www.coursera.org/articles/popular-cybersecurity-certifications) can affirm your skills and provide an advantage when applying for cybersecurity jobs. You may consider certification to boost your chances for employment in cybersecurity or take a step toward specializing in a particular area of the profession.


The[Security+](https://www.coursera.org/articles/what-is-the-comptia-security-plus-certification) is a common certification that you can earn through CompTIA. It establishes baseline skills and can help an entry-level cybersecurity professional learn more about cybersecurity work. For more experienced professionals, the[Certified Information Systems Security Professional](https://www.coursera.org/articles/cissp) (CISSP) validates experience with managing cybersecurity systems.
